claims.claim: Complement equivalence and exact endpoint cases. Let F(n,k) count labelled graphs on [n] with vertex-cover number at most k, let N=binom(n,2), and put m=n−k. For 0≤k≤n, F(n,k)=2^N−T(n,m), where T(n,m) is the number of labelled K_m-free graphs. Consequently F(n,n−3)=2^N−T(n,3), with T(n,3) the triangle-free graph count. Also F(n,0)=1; F(n,1)=1+n(2^{n−1}−1)−binom(n,2); F(n,n−2)=2^N−1; and F(n,n−1)=F(n,n)=2^N.
claims.evidence: For every graph, τ(G)=n−α(G), and complementation bijects graphs having an independent m-set with graphs containing K_m. The endpoint formulas follow directly; for k=1, nonempty star subgraphs are uniquely centered except that each one-edge graph is counted twice. Exact enumeration through n=6 confirmed all applicable identities.
claims.search_method: Independent bijective proof and exhaustive exact-integer enumeration; no web or unapproved evidence.

claims.claim: Two-sided family-size lower bounds. For 2≤m≤n, put r=m−1, write n=ar+s with 0≤s<r, and let e(n,m)=[n²−s(a+1)²−(r−s)a²]/2. Then T(n,m)≥2^{e(n,m)} and F(n,n−m)≥2^{N−binom(m,2)}. For fixed m≥3, e(n,m)=(m−2)n²/[2(m−1)]+O_m(1); specifically e(n,3)=floor(n²/4).
claims.evidence: All subgraphs of a fixed balanced complete (m−1)-partite graph are K_m-free, giving exactly 2^e graphs. Forcing the edges inside one fixed m-set to be absent gives 2^{N−binom(m,2)} graphs counted by F. Algebra gives e=(m−2)n²/[2(m−1)]−s(m−1−s)/[2(m−1)], proving the stated asymptotic and triangle case.
claims.search_method: Independent extremal construction and exact algebra, supplemented by exhaustive small-order checks.

claims.claim: Enumeration-strategy obstruction and its sharp endpoint boundary. For every fixed m≥3, both F(n,n−m) and T(n,m) have 2^{Θ(n²)} members. More generally, if m≥3 and k=n−m≥cn for a constant c>0, both families have 2^{Ω(n²)} members. Thus an algorithm that explicitly lists every admissible graph, or instead every K_m-free graph before subtracting from 2^N, cannot run in 2^{o(n²)} time in this regime. At m=2, T(n,2)=1, whereas at m=3 already T(n,3)≥2^{floor(n²/4)}; hence k=n−3 is the first fixed-distance-from-n endpoint where neither side can be explicitly enumerated within the target time. This does not prove a lower bound against implicit exact counting.
claims.evidence: Claim 1 and the 2^N upper bound prove the fixed-m statement. In the general regime, q=k(2n−k−1)/2≥k(n−1)/2=Ω(n²), while every subgraph of a balanced complete bipartite graph is K_m-free for m≥3. Explicit listing therefore needs at least one operation per family member. K_2-free graphs consist only of the edgeless graph, whereas the m=3 lower bound is quadratic-exponential. The draft correctly limits this obstruction to explicit enumeration.
claims.search_method: Manual asymptotic and computational-model analysis, with exact finite checks of the underlying bounds.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic exact algorithm using polynomial space and time 2^{q+O(n)}, where q=binom(n,2)−binom(n−k,2)=kn−k(k+1)/2. Therefore the target is achieved whenever k=o(n), including k=O(n/log n).
claims.evidence: For each k-set C there are exactly 2^q graphs with no edge outside C. Retaining a generated graph only for its first k-cover counts every graph with τ≤k exactly once, since any smaller cover extends to a k-cover. At most binom(n,k)^2 polynomial-time tests per generated edge pattern give 2^{q+O(n)} time, and enumeration plus an O(n²)-bit counter uses polynomial space. Since q≤nk, k=o(n) gives q=o(n²).
claims.search_method: Direct algorithm reconstruction and worst-case runtime/space accounting; exact q identities were checked computationally.

claims.claim: Structural hard-strip reduction. For n≥2 let ℓ(n)=floor(n/ceil(log₂n)). A deterministic exact 2^{o(n²)}-time algorithm for every 0≤k≤n exists if and only if one exists uniformly on the restricted strip ℓ(n)<k≤n−3. Equivalently, under m=n−k, the only unresolved range needed for the full target is 3≤m≤n−ℓ(n)−1.
claims.evidence: Restriction proves the forward implication. Conversely, k≤ℓ(n) is handled by Claim 3 with q≤n²/ceil(log₂n)=o(n²), k≥n−2 by the endpoint formulas, and every remaining integer lies in the stated strip. Substituting m=n−k gives exactly 3≤m≤n−ℓ(n)−1. Small-n overlaps and the partition were also checked exactly.
claims.search_method: Uniform case-partition proof and exact integer boundary checks.

claims.claim: For every fixed k there is a polynomial-time exact algorithm. More explicitly, F(n,k) is computable in time at most poly(n)·sum_{t=0}^k binom(n,t)·2^{binom(t,2)+t}·[2(t+2)]^{2^t−1}.
claims.evidence: For a cover C and I=V\C, any alternative cover corresponds to removing an H-independent X⊆C and adding at least U_X. Hence C is minimum exactly when |U_X|≥|X| for every such X. At equality the alternative minimum cover is (C\X)∪U_X, and the stated minimum-label condition is exactly the lexicographic tie-break. The capped-count/one-bit coordinates give the advertised finite state bound; summing over t, C, H, and neighborhood types yields the stated runtime and is polynomial for fixed k. Exhaustive testing over every graph through n=6 verified both the minimum and lex-first characterizations for every cover.
claims.search_method: Independent reconstruction of the cover-exchange bijection and DP, plus exhaustive exact testing.

claims.claim: Exact first- and second-moment formulas give certified bounds for all parameters. For 1≤m≤n, let q=N−binom(m,2), S1=binom(n,m)2^q, and S2=binom(n,m)·sum_{j=max(0,2m−n)}^m binom(m,j)binom(n−m,m−j)2^{N−2binom(m,2)+binom(j,2)}. Then max{2^q, ceil(S1²/S2)}≤F(n,n−m)≤min{2^N,S1}. In particular, q≤log₂F(n,n−m)≤q+n.
claims.evidence: With X(G) equal to the number of independent m-sets, direct double counting gives S1=Σ_G X(G). Ordered pairs intersecting in j vertices force exactly 2binom(m,2)−binom(j,2) absent edges, giving S2=Σ_G X(G)². The indicator bound and Cauchy–Schwarz yield the upper and second-moment lower bounds; fixing one independent m-set yields 2^q. Finally binom(n,m)≤2^n gives the logarithmic bracket. Exact enumeration through n=6 matched both moments and every bound.
claims.search_method: Independent double-counting and Cauchy–Schwarz proof with exhaustive exact-integer verification.

claims.claim: At the triangle-free endpoint, a substantial subclass is exactly countable in polynomial time. Let B_n be the number of labelled bipartite graphs and P_n=sum_{a=0}^n binom(n,a)2^{a(n−a)}. Then B_0=1 and B_n=(P_n−sum_{a=1}^{n−1}binom(n,a)B_aB_{n−a})/2. Hence F(n,n−3)≤2^N−B_n is an exact-arithmetic, polynomial-time computable bound.
claims.evidence: P_n counts bipartite graphs with an ordered proper two-coloring. A bipartite graph with c connected components has exactly 2^c such colorings, so the labelled EGFs satisfy P(x)=B(x)^2. Coefficient extraction isolates the two endpoint convolution terms and gives the recurrence. Since bipartite graphs are triangle-free, B_n≤T(n,3), yielding the asserted upper bound on F. The recurrence reproduced the exhaustive counts through n=6.
claims.search_method: Independent labelled-component/EGF derivation and exhaustive exact enumeration.

claims.claim: Direct distinguished-vertex recurrence for the triangle-free endpoint. Let 𝒯_r be the set of labelled triangle-free graphs on [r], and let i(H) include the empty set in the number of independent vertex sets of H. Then T(0,3)=1 and, for n≥1, T(n,3)=sum_{d=0}^{n−1} binom(n−1,d)·sum_{H∈𝒯_{n−1−d}} i(H)^d. Equivalently, T(n,3)=nT(n−1,3)+sum_{d=2}^{n−1} binom(n−1,d)·sum_{H∈𝒯_{n−1−d}} i(H)^d.
claims.evidence: After fixing a vertex v and its d-neighbor set S, triangle-freeness forces S independent. The residual graph H is triangle-free, and each s∈S independently chooses an independent neighborhood in H, producing i(H)^d reversible choices. The d=0 term is T(n−1,3), while Σ_{H∈𝒯_{n−2}}i(H)=T(n−1,3), so the d=1 term is (n−1)T(n−1,3). Both recurrences exactly reproduced all triangle-free counts through n=6.
claims.search_method: Independent reversible decomposition around a distinguished vertex and exhaustive exact verification.

claims.claim: The distinguished-vertex recurrence gives a deterministic exact algorithm for F(n,n−3) in time poly(n)·2^{binom(n−3,2)} with exponential space, or time poly(n)·2^{binom(n−2,2)} with polynomial space, for n≥3. Both exponents remain Θ(n²), so neither algorithm achieves the requested 2^{o(n²)} strength.
claims.evidence: Only moments on r≤n−3 vertices occur after combining d=0,1. The subset-zeta construction correctly gives i(H)=g(complement E(H)) for every H in poly(r)·2^{binom(r,2)} time and space. Recomputing i(H) from its 2^r vertex subsets instead uses polynomial space and exponent binom(r,2)+r, maximized at r=n−3 as binom(n−2,2). Bottom-up smaller orders add only polynomial factors, and all integers have O(n²) bits. Exhaustive checking verified the zeta identity for every graph through r=5.
claims.search_method: Independent recurrence-dependency, zeta-transform, bit-complexity, and exponent analysis with exhaustive exact verification.

target_evidence: The draft does not prove the complete source target. It gives correct exact algorithms for k=o(n), fixed k, and trivial near-n endpoints, plus valid reductions, bounds, and Θ(n²)-exponent triangle-endpoint algorithms. It explicitly leaves the uniform strip ℓ(n)<k≤n−3 unresolved, including k=n−3, and therefore accurately claims only partial progress rather than a uniform 2^{o(n²)} algorithm.
